questions.q: What makes a landing zone different from simply handing a team a blank subscription or account?
options: It arrives pre-wired with identity, networking, logging, and policy guardrails already active before any workload deploys
It is identical to a blank subscription, just renamed for marketing purposes
It only applies to production environments, never to dev or test
It removes the need for any identity or access controls entirely
questions.explain: A landing zone is a pre-configured, pre-governed environment — governance is the starting state, not something configured (or forgotten) after a team starts deploying into a blank subscription.

questions.q: Under Azure Landing Zones, what does the Platform management group typically contain?
options: Shared-services subscriptions like Management, Connectivity, and Identity
Every individual workload subscription in the company
Only sandbox subscriptions used for experimentation
A single subscription containing all resources company-wide
questions.explain: The Platform management group holds the shared-services subscriptions — Management (logging/monitoring), Connectivity (shared networking), and Identity (if needed) — that every workload subscription depends on.

questions.q: What is AWS Control Tower's Account Factory responsible for?
options: Provisioning new AWS accounts pre-wired with the organization's guardrails already active
Manually configuring IAM policies one account at a time after the account is created
Deleting unused AWS accounts automatically after 90 days
Generating billing reports across all accounts in the organization
questions.explain: Account Factory is Control Tower's mechanism for vending new accounts that already have the organization's preventive and detective guardrails active from the moment they're created — the AWS parallel to a subscription landing under Azure's Landing Zones management group.

questions.q: In AWS Control Tower's landing zone setup, why is the Log Archive account kept separate from accounts doing actual work?
options: To centralize and protect audit logs from being altered or deleted by whoever has access to a workload account
Because AWS requires every account to have a matching log archive account for billing purposes
Because workload accounts aren't allowed to generate any logs at all
To reduce AWS's own storage costs, with no governance benefit to the customer
questions.explain: A dedicated, separate Log Archive account keeps the audit trail centralized and tamper-resistant — someone with access to a workload account can't alter or erase the logs documenting what happened in it.

questions.q: Why does the lesson say a dedicated data/analytics landing zone matters specifically for data governance?
options: It can pre-apply data-specific policy — like mandatory encryption or mandatory classification tags — automatically to every data workload that lands in it
Data workloads don't require any governance guardrails, unlike other workload types
A dedicated data landing zone eliminates the need for any identity or access management
AWS Control Tower and Azure Landing Zones only work for data workloads, not general compute
questions.explain: A dedicated data landing zone branch lets an organization pre-apply data-specific guardrails (mandatory encryption, no public storage access, mandatory classification tagging) automatically to every workload that lands there, the same way general landing zones pre-apply baseline security policy.
